title: Stein's Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: Every oriented graph $G$ with $\delta^{0}(G)>k/2$ contains every orientation of the $k$-edge path.
context_text: Stein conjectured this as a generalization of Jackson's theorem on directed paths in oriented graphs with minimum semidegree at least $k/2$. The conjecture has been confirmed for directed paths (Jackson), for oriented graphs without oriented 4-cycles (Stein–Trujillo-Negrete), and partially for antidirected paths (Klimošová–Stein, Chen–Hou–Zhou, Skokan–Tyomkyn).
paper_contribution: Proves that every oriented graph $G$ satisfying an explicit semidegree lower bound (depending on block sizes $\ell$ and $k-\ell$) contains every two-block oriented path with $k$ arcs, and in particular that $\delta^{0}(G)\geq 3k/4$ suffices for all two-block paths, extending the evidence for Stein's conjecture.
paper_title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs of large semidegree

title: Question 5.1
statement_text: Is it true that every oriented graph $G$ with $\delta^{0}(G)\geq k/2$ contains every orientation of the $k$-edge path, save for the antidirected orientations?
context_text: An oriented graph is a digraph with no loops and no directed cycles of length two; its minimum semidegree $\delta^0(G)$ is the minimum over all vertices of the in- and out-degrees. An orientation of the $k$-edge path is antidirected if consecutive arcs alternate in direction. Stein conjectured that every oriented graph with $\delta^0(G)>k/2$ contains every orientation of the $k$-edge path; Jackson proved this for directed paths (even with $\delta^0(G)\ge k/2$), and it is known for antidirected paths under stronger bounds (down to about $\frac12(k-1+\sqrt{k-3})$). The authors prove the case of paths with two blocks (maximal directed subpaths) under semidegree conditions, e.g. $\delta^0(G)\ge3k/4$ suffices for every two-block path with $k$ arcs. The $(k/2)$-blow-up of a directed cycle has $\delta^0=k/2$ and no antidirected $k$-arc path, and a regular tournament on $k+1$ vertices ($k$ even) has $\delta^0=k/2$ and, by Havet and Thomassé, contains every oriented $k$-arc path except (three small exceptions involving) the antidirected one, which motivated this question in an earlier version. In the final version the authors observe that the blow-up of a directed cycle in fact excludes every bouncing path for even $k$ (a path $p_0\dots p_k$ in which the two arcs $p_{2i}p_{2i+1}$ and $p_{2i+1}p_{2i+2}$ have opposite directions for every $i$, a class strictly containing the antidirected paths when $k\ge4$), so the question as stated has a negative answer for even $k\ge4$; they replace it by: does $\delta^0(G)\ge k/2$ force every orientation of the $k$-edge path except the bouncing paths when $k$ is even?
paper_title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs of large semidegree
